A standing read on what WATA's published schedule actually delivers — frequency by hour, by route. This is what the timetable promises; whether buses actually keep it is Panel 02, and it's still early days there.

Weekday frequency by hour

01
ScopeMedian minutes between departures per route per hour, computed at each route's busiest stop on the weekday (Full-Weekday) service pattern. Blank cells mean no scheduled service that hour, which is different from infrequent service. Every route starts from the Williamsburg Transit Center — the same building as the Amtrak station — except the four marked *; see below for where those actually begin.
Less frequent More frequent

Every route's first scheduled stop, in at least one direction, is N Boundary St at Williamsburg TC — the Williamsburg Transit Center, which shares its building with the Amtrak station — except four, marked * above: Route 8 (W&M) loops the campus between WM Grad Plex and the School of Education; Route 4 (Longhill) runs between New Town Ave at Velocity and E Rochambeau Dr at Wal-Mart; Route 9 (Toano) runs between Barhamsville Rd at LaGrange Pkwy and E Rochambeau Dr at Wal-Mart; Route 11 (Yorktown) runs between Battery Blvd at Riverside Hospital and Barham Blvd at Rivermeade. None of the four ever reaches the Transit Center, in either direction, per stop_times.txt.

On-time performance

02
ScopeThis panel is deliberately empty. Reliability is measured by polling the Transit API every 30 minutes and comparing against the archived schedule; nothing is published here until the sample is large enough to be worth reading.

Still collecting

Real-time polling started 20 Sep 2026. On-time figures need roughly three weeks of accumulated data before a bad week can be told apart from a bad route, so nothing is reported here yet.

Real-time predictions were found to populate only in the last ~10 minutes before a trip's departure — at 30-minute polling, expect a live reading on only about a third of trips. The rest fall back to schedule-only and are excluded from on-time figures rather than miscounted as "on time."

What will appear here

  • On-time performance (−1/+5 min window), by route and hour
  • Delay distributions, so a consistently-late route reads differently from an occasionally-very-late one
  • Cancellations, tracked separately from trips that simply weren't observed
  • Real-time capture rate, published alongside every figure — not every trip gets a live reading

How these numbers were made

Everything above comes from two sources: WATA's published GTFS schedule feed and a live poll of the Transit API. Both have limits worth knowing before the figures are quoted anywhere.

Schedule data

GTFS feed snapshot dated 2026-09-18, covering 12 active routes (route 12A is defined but currently unserved). Trip counts are exact reads of stop_times.txt, both directions combined.

Service days come entirely from calendar_dates.txt exceptions — the feed's own calendar.txt is always empty. The feed's forward-looking window is roughly one month, so it's re-archived weekly.

Frequency

Median minutes between departures, computed at each route's single busiest stop to avoid conflating branches or directions. An hour with no scheduled service is left blank, distinct from a scheduled trip that simply runs infrequently.

Coverage

Walk bands are 800-meter straight-line buffers around every one of the 303 stops actually served by a trip (of 614 stops defined in the feed). Tiered by weekday departure volume at that stop, then dissolved by tier to avoid double-counting overlapping buffers.

Reliability

Polls the Transit API's stop_departures endpoint roughly every 30 minutes during service hours, using a fixed core of ~48 stops (covering every route and direction every poll) plus a rotating sample across the network's other ~255 stops.

Real-time predictions (is_real_time=true) were found to populate only in the last ~10 minutes before departure, so 30-minute polling catches a live reading on only about a third of trips. No on-time figure is published until roughly three weeks of collection have accumulated.

What is not measured

Ridership, crowding, fare payment, paratransit trips and vehicle condition are all outside this dashboard. A route with high trip counts and full coverage can still run mostly empty, and nothing here would show it.

Figures on this page are generated from open data and carry the limits described above. WATA's own Swiftly GTFS-RT feed (vehicle positions) is not part of this pipeline — the Transit API is the sole real-time source. This dashboard is independent and is not published by the Williamsburg Area Transit Authority.

Where the network reaches
